topPRs.title: delta: rename contract_creation_bits to zero_to_bits
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #944 — **base is `gk/lagoon-span-batch-post-exec`, not `main`.** Review after #944, or read [the single commit](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/944/commits) for this change alone. Retarget to `main` once #944 merges.

Requested in [#944 review](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/944#discussion_r4014708102).

## Why

`contract_creation_bits` is named for a condition it does not test. What the bit governs is whether a transaction consumes an entry from `tx_tos`: a `0` bit consumes the next address, a `1` bit consumes none. For every transaction type that has a `to` field, "is a contract creation" and "has no `to`" coincide — so the name has been accurate by luck rather than by construction.

The Lagoon post-exec transaction (`0x7D`) is the first type where they come apart. It has no `to` field and is not a contract creation, so it sets a bit whose documented meaning is false of it. Specifying that in #944 took a paragraph of apology; this rename removes the need for it, and that paragraph goes away here.

## Why `zero_to_bits` and not `nonzero_to_bits`

The name first suggested would invert the meaning. The bit is `1` when the `to` is *absent*; `nonzero_to_bits` reads as `1` = `to` is present, so a find-and-replace would silently flip the sense for anyone reading it fresh. `zero_to_bits` keeps the polarity. `no_to_bits` and `to_omitted_bits` would do equally well — it is a one-line change if either reads better.

Flipping the bit *and* renaming would read best of all, but that is a wire change rather than a rename, and not worth a fork gate.

## Why this is safe

Purely editorial. Nothing in a span batch is self-describing — `txs` is a positional concatenation (`zero_to_bits ++ y_parity_bits ++ tx_sigs ++ ...`) with no tags or field names on the wire. The encoding, the bit polarity and every derived chain are untouched, and no fork gate is involved.

Edits a shipped fork document, so the Delta text keeps a note recording the former name, which keeps searches and third-party implementations landing in the right place.

Client identifiers (`contractCreationBits` in op-node, `contract_creation_bits` in kona) can follow whenever convenient. Nothing breaks while spec and code vocabulary differ — this is a comment-level mismatch, not an interface one.

## Changes

- `specs/protocol/delta/span-batches.md` — the field definition (reworded to describe what the bit actually selects), the `txs` layout line, the decode-ordering note, and the `tx_tos` parsing note. Plus the former-name note.
- `specs/protocol/lagoon/derivation.md` — renamed heading, table row and cross-reference; the explanatory paragraph collapses from seven lines to two, which was the point.

`markdownlint`, `doctoc`, `cspell` and the filename check all pass.
